questions: Should the function raise FileNotFoundError only if the script file does not exist, or also if the file exists but is not a valid Python script or cannot be executed?
Is the timeout measured in seconds, and does it include the time to start the subprocess and any overhead, or only the execution time of the script?
Should the function terminate only the specific subprocess launched, or also any child processes it may have spawned?
If the script completes successfully but the subprocess returns a non-zero exit code, should it still return 'Script executed successfully.'?
Is the script always executed with the command ['python', script_path], or should it use sys.executable or allow other interpreters?
Should the function handle keyboard interrupts (Ctrl+C) during execution, and if so, what should be returned?
If the script path contains spaces or special characters, should it be escaped in the subprocess call and pkill command?
Should the function ensure thread cleanup after termination to avoid zombie threads or resource leaks?
